submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on the closing, non-initial piece of a whitespace-free spelling unit that began at an earlier token: the final sub-word fragment of a word the tokenizer split ('ated' in irrit|ated, 'ulated' in congrat|ulated, 'ened' in hast|ened), the closing fragment of a markup element ('</', ';/', '></', ':/'), the inner pieces and tail of a numeric or identifier string ('05/11/2001', 'arXiv:0805.2410', '11:27:23'), and the newline that terminates a Wikipedia 'Category:' metadata line; it stays near its floor on ordinary space-initial English words in running prose, so swapping a split word for a one-token synonym ('irritated' -> 'annoyed', 'percolated' -> 'seeped') roughly halves or removes the peak. Label a position predicted-active when its token is a non-initial fragment of a unit (word, tag, number, metadata field) that started at an earlier token, and predicted-inactive when it is a space-initial ordinary word in mid-clause with no such unit open.

rival_explanations: The pole is an affective/experiencer-predicate neuron: it fires on past-participle psych verbs ('startled', 'convinced', 'disappointed', 'annoyed', 'irritated') and the markup, date and Code-token peaks are incidental spillover, so it predicts activity for 'the news shocked the panel' but none for '05/11/2001' or ' '.

The pole is a plain non-word-token detector: it fires on any token that does not begin a whitespace-delimited word (digit groups, symbol fragments, whitespace runs, byte-fallback and word-internal fragments), so it predicts activity at every non-space-initial token inside code, numbers and non-Latin/foreign text and none on any space-initial token, including ' startled'.

The pole is narrower than I claim: it fires only on markup closers and on digit groups inside multi-part numbers, and its word-fragment peaks are a separate mechanism, so it predicts inactivity on 'congratulated' and 'hastened' in plain prose while still firing on '' and '05/11/2001'.

top_examples.text:
The Bombers survived penalties to beat St. Thomas More 2-1 in the final.
Jun. 4, 2016 7:00 a.m.
The L.V. Rogers girls soccer team has won a provincial championship.
An undefeated season concluded the only way it could for the L.V. Rogers girls soccer team — with a provincial championship.
The Bombers survived a penalty shootout to defeat Burnaby’s St. Thomas More Knights 2-1 in the gold-medal final at the BC High School Girls AA Soccer championships in Campbell River on Saturday.
Maya Ida scored the winning goal on the seventh shot of the shootout and Naomi Perkins scored in regulation as the Bombers won the provincial title for the first time since taking back-to-back championships in 1997 and 1998, respectively.
Perkins was named tournament MVP and awarded the Golden Boot for scoring 10 goals during the tournament.
It’s the second provincial title for Nelson’s high school in a week after the senior boys rugby team won gold on May 28.
LVR was under pressure early. The Knights scored on a free kick under 10 minutes into the game, putting the Bombers in the rare spot of having to play from behind.
The Bombers tied the game before the half was over on a corner kick. Laurel Halleran found Perkins, who fired the ball off her left foot to beat the opposing keeper in the far corner.
That set up a rollicking final 40 minutes after the break.
Bennett credited goalkeeper Hanna Quinn with keeping her team alive.
Quinn’s best save came in the dying minutes of regulation. The Knights strong midfield fired a shot that Quinn had to leap across the width of the goal to get a hand on and keep LVR alive .
Perkins, meanwhile, had to leave the game briefly after suffering a head injury fighting for a ball in the air. She was assessed by a physio on the sidelines and told she could return to play, which she did for extra time.
A scoreless extra time meant penalties for both teams. On the fifth shooter, the Knights had a chance to win but their shooter hit the crossbar. Two shooters later, Ida put the Bombers ahead on a shot to the top corner.
Quinn then guessed right, with a terrific save to deny the Knights and seal the Bombers’ title.

est un film américain réalisé par Sofia Coppola, sorti en 2010.

Synopsis 
La scène d'ouverture commence avec une Ferrari noire circulant sur un circuit dans le désert, le moteur rugissant à chaque tour. Quand la voiture stoppe, Johnny Marco (Stephen Dorff) en sort. Marco est un acteur à succès à Hollywood qui, en dépit de son ascension, n'aime pas ce qu'est devenue sa vie. Trentenaire, il tourne essentiellement des films commerciaux.

Johnny réside au Château Marmont sur le Sunset boulevard, fréquenté par le Tout Hollywood.  Il voit débarquer sa fille de 11 ans, Cleo (Elle Fanning).

معبد كل الأديان (بالروسية: Храм всех религий) أو المعبد العالمي (بالروسية: Вселенский храм) هو المجمع المعماري في مدينة قازان في روسيا. الزعيم الروحي والمصمم للمعبد هو إلدار خانوف سبب إنشاء المعبد هو حادثة رجوع إلدار إلى الحياة بحسب اعتقاد والداه في حادثة غريبة عام 1943، فأراد إلدار شكر «الله» ببناء معبد لكل الأديان بحسب زعمه. تم البدأ بتشييد هيكل المعبد عام 1994، ومازال قيد الإنشاء. يتكون الهيكل من عدة أنواع من العمارة الدينية بما في ذلك الكنيسة الأرثوذكسية، والمسجد، والكنيس اليهودي. يقدم الهيكل كمركز ثقافي وإقامة.

readings.explanation: The pole fires on the closing, non-initial piece of a whitespace-free spelling unit that began at an earlier token: the final sub-word fragment of a word the tokenizer split ('ated' in irrit|ated, 'ulated' in congrat|ulated, 'ened' in hast|ened), the closing fragment of a markup element ('</', ';/', '></', ':/'), the inner pieces and tail of a numeric or identifier string ('05/11/2001', 'arXiv:0805.2410', '11:27:23'), and the newline that terminates a Wikipedia 'Category:' metadata line; it stays near its floor on ordinary space-initial English words in running prose, so swapping a split word for a one-token synonym ('irritated' -> 'annoyed', 'percolated' -> 'seeped') roughly halves or removes the peak. Label a position predicted-active when its token is a non-initial fragment of a unit (word, tag, number, metadata field) that started at an earlier token, and predicted-inactive when it is a space-initial ordinary word in mid-clause with no such unit open.

The pole is an affective/experiencer-predicate neuron: it fires on past-participle psych verbs ('startled', 'convinced', 'disappointed', 'annoyed', 'irritated') and the markup, date and Code-token peaks are incidental spillover, so it predicts activity for 'the news shocked the panel' but none for '05/11/2001' or ' '.

The pole is a plain non-word-token detector: it fires on any token that does not begin a whitespace-delimited word (digit groups, symbol fragments, whitespace runs, byte-fallback and word-internal fragments), so it predicts activity at every non-space-initial token inside code, numbers and non-Latin/foreign text and none on any space-initial token, including ' startled'.

The pole is narrower than I claim: it fires only on markup closers and on digit groups inside multi-part numbers, and its word-fragment peaks are a separate mechanism, so it predicts inactivity on 'congratulated' and 'hastened' in plain prose while still firing on '' and '05/11/2001'.
